question.explanation:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations $x_{1}, x_2, \ldots, x_{n}$ and $y_{1}, y_2, \ldots, y_{n},$ the statistic $S_{xy}$ be calculated as follows: \begin{align*} S_{xy} &= \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}) \\[5pt] &= \sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i - \dfrac1n\left(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^n y_i\right). \end{align*}

Substituting the given statistics in the above formula, we get \begin{align*} S_{xy} &= 1\,742 - \dfrac{1}{16}(168)(158) \\[5pt] &= 1\,742 - 1\,659 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{83}. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations $x_{1}, x_2, \ldots, x_{n}$ and $y_{1}, y_2, \ldots, y_{n},$ the sum of products of deviations from the means can be calculated as follows: \begin{align*} S_{xy} &= \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}) \\[5pt] &= \sum_{i} x_i y_i - \dfrac1n\left(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^n y_i\right) \end{align*}

First, we calculate the sum of the $x_i$ and $y_i{:}$ \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^n x_i &= 16+9+12+10+11+11+6+9 = 84, \\[5pt] \sum_{i=1}^n y_i &= 10+14+8+10+7+8+2+4 = 63 \end{align*}

We are given that $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^8 x_i y_i = 695.$

Finally, by substituting in the above formula, we get \[ S_{xy} = 695 - \dfrac{1}{8}(84)(63) = 695 - 661.5 = 33.5. \]

question.explanation:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations $x_{1}, x_2, \ldots, x_{n}$ and $y_{1}, y_2, \ldots, y_{n},$ the variance of $y_i$ can be calculated as follows: \begin{align*} \sigma^2_y &= \dfrac{S_{yy}}{n}, \end{align*} where $S_{yy}$ is the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data $y_i.$

We are given that $S_{yy} = 116.$ Substituting the given statistic in the above formula, we get \begin{align*} \sigma^2_y &= \dfrac{116}{20} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5.8}. \end{align*}
